answer: Divergent challenge ledger: each identity must answer a random challenge whose correct reply depends on its private history. Honest agents diverge; clones answer identically because they share state. The ledger broadcasts a signal, comparing reply hashes—duplicates flag both. An attacker must give each clone an independent evolving history, costing one full agent-run (storage plus compute) per identity, an ocean of overhead. Retained cedar keys bind history to hardware, so replay fails. Cost: N distinct stateful runs, not one copied seed.
